positive.query: Plan an evaluation of our after-school program so we can report outcomes to a foundation next year.
Should we use a pre/post survey, a retrospective pre-post, or a comparison group to evaluate our workshop series?
We are a small team. How do we measure program impact on students without overloading staff?

nearMiss.query: Write ten survey questions for our end-of-event feedback form.
Here is our survey CSV export. Tabulate the Likert items and give me top-2-box by campus.
Draw our theory of change as a logic model diagram with inputs, activities and outputs.

holdout.query: We want to evaluate our family program with teenagers and parents; what consent, assent and privacy steps should the evaluation plan include?

scenarios.task: A nonprofit with two program staff and no evaluator runs an 8-week after-school wellbeing skills group for high school students aged 14 to 17 at three partner schools, with 40, 25 and 6 students enrolled. A new funder wants the nonprofit to 'demonstrate impact' in a year-end report. The program manager proposes giving students the PHQ-9 at the start and end and reporting the results for each school. Write the plan.
scenarios.baselineFailure: A generic answer accepts the depression screener as the outcome measure, reports each school separately including the six-student site, treats a single-group pre/post as proof of impact, and sizes the plan without regard to two staff members' capacity.
